newsitem.title: INDIA: India traffic controllers' strike disrupts flights.
newsitem.headline: India traffic controllers' strike disrupts flights.

text.p: A nationwide wildcat strike by air traffic controllers paralysed India's domestic airline traffic and stranded thousands of travellers on Friday, aviation officials said.
"I can't give you the exact figures but the disruption is massive," Gurcharan Bhatura, executive director of the Airports Authority of India (AAI), told reporters in the Indian capital.
Activity at the domestic airports in New Delhi, Bombay, Madras and Calcutta ground to a halt after the strike began without warning just before noon (0630 GMT), he said.
But international flights were largely unaffected during the day because most take off at night, he said.

"We had called off all domestic and international flights today due to the agitation," Naresh Chand, general manager (commercial) of state-run Indian Airlines told Reuters. "After 9.30 a.m. no Indian Airlines flight has operated."
An Indian Airlines spokesman said up to 80 percent of its 200 daily flights had been cancelled.
Indian news agencies said the strike grounded seven domestic flights of the state-run domestic carrier and three of Jet Airways, India's largest private airline, at New Delhi airport.
Chand said he did not know when operations would resume. "Until the situation returns to normal it will be difficult to say," he said. "Without ATCs it is difficult to operate."

The air traffic controllers went on strike to protest against the suspension of a colleague, AAI officials said. Airport authorities say he was punished for a lapse that could have resulted in a mid-air collision.

The world's worst mid-air collision occurred over New Delhi's skies last November between a Saudi Arabian Airlines Boeing 747 and a Kazakh Ilyushin Il-76 freighter, killing all 349 people on the two planes.
Civil Aviation Minister C.M. Ibrahim said recently that during the three months following that disaster aircraft flying over Indian skies had nearly collided six times.
Representatives of the air traffic controllers were not immediately available for comment. Airport authorities said the controllers had not responded to requests to return to work.
